subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

judge.implied_focus: Perceived airline service quality across specific experience dimensions (seat, crew, food, customer service, value, aircraft), extracted from free-text reviews

per_column.name: seat_comfort_quality
per_column.rationale: An ordinal quality facet of the airline experience, extracted from review text and centred on service/experience quality.

per_column.name: cabin_crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A coherent service-quality facet on a consistent ordinal scale.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Another experience facet aligned to the same quality-assessment framing.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Service-responsiveness facet, coherent with the overall service-quality focus.

per_column.name: value_for_money
per_column.rationale: Value perception facet; a recognised dimension of overall satisfaction, on an ordinal scale.

per_column.name: aircraft_type_condition
per_column.rationale: Hardware/condition facet of the flight experience, consistent with the quality-facet structure.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively centre on ONE coherent, data-inferable focus: perceived service/experience quality decomposed into distinct experience facets, all rendered on consistent ordinal quality scales inferred from review text. This is not a scattered grab-bag nor a set of mechanical text metrics, satisfying focus_coherence well. The structure is sound: multiple differentiated facets at a useful granularity that an analyst could compare against Overall Rating / Recommended to find the most influential aspect — directly serving the 'which aspect is most worth analyzing' intent, giving good actionability. The main weakness lowering structure_quality is redundancy with existing structured rating columns (Seat Comfort, Staff Service, Food & Beverages, Value For Money already exist), so several added facets largely restate columns already present rather than adding genuinely new decomposition; the more novel contributions are customer_service_responsiveness and aircraft_type_condition. The set still forms a usable predictor/attribute structure around a clear focus, but the overlap and lack of any explicit target/salience column keeps it short of an ideal analytical scaffold.
